clue.text: Forbidding plump women chasing back speaker who crossed the Atlantic

indicators.note: chasing puts the forbidding plump women behind the turned speaker, following it
back tells us to read the speaker's word from its end to its start

parts.note: the lip is an organ of speech, so a speaker in a loose sense
forbidding means grim, stern-looking
plump means fat
women's belongings are hers

explanation.surface: Stern stout ladies pursue a talker who has made an ocean crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: The lip is an organ of speech, so it stands loosely for a speaker; 'back' turns it and 'chasing' sets the rest behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pilgrim Fathers were the English settlers who sailed to America in 1620, so they are people who crossed the Atlantic.

clue.text: Idler composed German song about American president

indicators.note: about means the song goes round the president

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song
Abe is Abraham Lincoln, an American president

explanation.surface: A lazy person composed a German song about Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-abed is someone who lazes in bed late, an idler.

clue.text: 10 on beast can be expressed as a fraction

definitions.text: can be expressed as a fraction

indicators.note: on places the ten after the beast in this down entry

parts.note: a rat is a beast
the figures one and zero look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Ten on an animal can be written as a fraction.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a reference to 10 across but is read as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is a quantitative relation that can be written as one number over another.

clue.text: 1 5's craft is quite likely to prosper

parts.note: may expresses likelihood, as in it may rain
to flower is to flourish, prosper

explanation.surface: The Pilgrim Fathers' ship is likely to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 5 is PILGRIM FATHERS, who sailed on the Mayflower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower was the ship that carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620.

clue.text: See 1
Somewhat fuddled, I reach South American territory

indicators.note: somewhat means only a portion, the opening part, of the next word is taken

parts.note: ego is Latin for I

explanation.surface: Somewhat drunk, I arrive at the tip of South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' takes FU from 'fuddled'. Tierra del Fuego is the archipelago at South America's southern tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuego is short for Tierra del Fuego, the territory at South America's southern tip.

clue.text: Arrogant female perhaps and crucial male in turn

indicators.note: in means the crucial male goes inside the turn

parts.note: taken as written
key means crucial, vital
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A proud woman and a vital man take their turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey hen is a female turkey, and turkeys are proverbially strutting and arrogant.

clue.text: He turns out to be a winner under direction

indicators.note: under puts the winner below the direction in this down entry

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: He proves to be a champion under guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' looks like 'proves to be' but is the verb for expelling someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor is a person who throws tenants out of a property.

clue.text: How far can the street go with its French counterpart a laughing stock? The answer is really unexpected

parts.words: How far can the street go
parts.note: ST for street plus range, how far something can go
a butt is the target of jokes
rue is French for street

explanation.surface: Asking how far a street and its Parisian equivalent can go, the reply is surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The French counterpart of street is RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange but true describes a fact that is genuinely surprising, really unexpected.

clue.text: Danger point for space traveller axing ecological endeavour

indicators.note: axing chops the head off the ecological endeavour, losing its opening letter

parts.note: green means environmentally friendly, ecological
an endeavour is a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: An environmental project is cancelled, a hazard for an astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axing' removes the G at the head of GREEN TRY, leaving REENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-entry into the atmosphere is the most perilous moment of a spacecraft's return to Earth.

clue.text: Noble that is royal before

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A nobleman who is royal comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier and before are synonyms, both meaning at a previous time.

clue.text: Setter's relative energy encompasses student on first row

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself says I am, shortened to I'm
bro is short for brother, a relative

indicators.note: encompasses means the energy word goes round the student-and-first piece

parts.note: go means energy, vigour

indicators.note: on puts the student next to the first, the student coming before it

parts.note: L is a learner driver, a student
I is the Roman numeral one, first

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler's kin has the vigour to put a pupil in the front row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' is the compiler talking about himself, so it gives I'M; 'encompasses' wraps the energy word round student plus first.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused quarrel or entanglement, a row in the sense of a noisy dispute.

clue.text: School report saying "Rusty"?

indicators.note: a report says something aloud, so the school's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school report describes a pupil as rusty.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON, the English boarding school, said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eaten away by corrosion is rusty, as metal is eaten by rust.

clue.text: Glory acquired by repelling vulgar derogation of the country

indicators.note: repelling pushes the words back, so the pieces read from end to start

parts.note: sod is a vulgar term of abuse
UK is the United Kingdom, the country

explanation.surface: Fame is won by fending off crude insults to the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise and renown, a synonym for glory.

clue.text: Intersection at Bologna, perhaps

parts.note: a tangled road junction nicknamed after a pasta dish served bolognese

explanation.surface: A road junction in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Spaghetti Junction is the nickname of a famous tangled motorway interchange in Birmingham, England; spaghetti bolognese supplies Bologna.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaghetti junction is a complex intersection, and the pasta is typically served bolognese.

clue.text: Boxer of Animal Farm, with a turn for the right where one went on the parish

indicators.text: with a turn for the right
indicators.note: a U-turn is a turn, and here the letter U gives way to R for right

parts.words: where one went on the parish
parts.note: a pauper living on parish relief was sent to the workhouse

explanation.surface: A character from Orwell's novel takes a right turn where paupers once went.
explanation.walkthrough: In Orwell's Animal Farm, Boxer is the loyal, overworked carthorse. Going on the parish meant living on parish poor relief, often in a WORKHOUSE; its U (a turn) becomes R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer, the tireless carthorse of Orwell's fable, is the very model of a hard-working horse.

clue.text: Put off coming up with a gamble as entry that's well thought of

indicators.note: as entry means the gamble goes into the turned word
coming up means the word rises, read from bottom to top in this down entry

parts.note: to deter is to put off
a spec is a speculation, a gamble

explanation.surface: Postponed, coming up with a bet as entry is well regarded.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'coming up' reads the word from the bottom upwards; 'as entry' slips the gamble inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Respected means held in high esteem, well thought of.

clue.text: Roget on the Lizard?

parts.note: saurus is Greek for lizard, as in dinosaur names

explanation.surface: Roget writes about the Lizard peninsula in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lizard looks like the Cornish peninsula but gives the Greek SAURUS. Roget compiled the famous Thesaurus.
explanation.definitionFit: Roget is the name of the most famous English thesaurus, so his name stands for the book.

clue.text: Name for what (or two) he has?

definitions.text: Name for what (or two) he has?

parts.note: a rich man has a bob or two, a bob being an old shilling

explanation.surface: Here is a name for someone with a bob or two to his name.
explanation.walkthrough: A BOB was a shilling in old British money; 'a bob or two' means plenty of cash, which a rich man has.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a very rich man, originally one made wealthy in India, who has a bob or two.

clue.text: This bloomer could be a big one

definitions.text: This bloomer could be a big one

indicators.note: could be suggests these letters may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: This flower might be a large specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' signals the anagram of A BIG ONE. 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The begonia is a flowering plant, so a bloomer.

Race in Kashmir is hard run

run marks the letters as one unbroken run across those words

explanation.surface: A race in Kashmir is a difficult run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish are a people or nation, and race is used loosely for such a people.

clue.text: Little Sir from "Never on Sunday"?

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A small knight appears in the film Never on Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: Never on Sunday is a 1960 film title, but read literally it describes a night from Monday to Friday, not the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: A weeknight is any night except at the weekend, so it is never on a Sunday.

clue.text: Acquire companion by helicopter?

parts.note: to win is to gain, acquire
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Picking up a friend by helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Rescuers lift people up by cable from a helicopter with a hoist, gaining a passenger.

explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' signals the anagram of TRANSIT.

clue.text: Time for a somewhat aged and 16 27 composer

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the aged word is used, its tail dropped

parts.note: venerable means old and revered

explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' cuts ABLE from VENERABLE, leaving VENER. 16 and 27 are RESPECTED and ENGLISH; John Tavener was an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Tavener was a highly regarded English composer of sacred music.

clue.text: His age combined with idleness caused under-production

indicators.note: combined says the letters of the two phrases are mixed together

explanation.surface: Getting older together with laziness led to falling output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combined' signals the anagram of HIS AGE IDLENESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was a 1970s label for Britain's low industrial productivity and strikes.
